geo.label: March lift-off priced, half-point debated
parts: Macro Stance

The US enters Wednesday with a relief rally sitting on an unresolved inflation problem. Moscow's claim that it has begun a partial troop pullback from the Ukraine border, met by NATO calls for caution, as CNBC reported, flipped Tuesday's tape. [[n1497]] The S&P 500 rose +1.58% to 4,471.07 index points, the Nasdaq 100 +2.47% to 14,620.82 index points and the Russell 2000 +2.75%, while the VIX fell 2.63 points to 25.70 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). January consumer prices rose 7.5% on an annual basis, more than expected and the highest since 1982, according to CNBC, and the S&P 500 is still -2.32% over 20 sessions. [[n2108]] Stance Mixed: a geopolitical discount is being removed, not a macro all-clear, and the Fed is tightening into an equity multiple that has not finished adjusting.
Rates & Curve

Prior-close Treasury par yields put the 2Y at 1.58% and the 10Y at 2.05%, a 10Y-2Y spread of +47 bps on a positively sloped curve (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-15). Over 20 observations the 2Y has risen 52 bps from 1.06% and the 10Y 18 bps from 1.87%, compressing the spread by 34 bps: a bear flattening, with both legs up and the 2Y up more. The last five observations alone added 23 bps at the 2Y and 9 bps at the 10Y. Reuters described a curve that prices Fed tightening and shows fears of policy error. [[n2213]] The 10Y topping 2% for the first time since 2019 after hot inflation, as CNBC reported, put duration back in the crosshairs, and TLT fell -1.14% even as equities rallied (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). [[n2170]] With the 3M at 0.40% and the 10Y-3M spread at +165 bps, the front end still has room to reprice if March delivers more than a quarter point.
New / Most Important

The most important new input is the debate over the size of the first move. A Reuters poll has the Fed raising rates 25 bps in March, but with calls for 50 bps growing louder. [[n1367]] Bullard reiterated his rate comments as the dollar gained on Ukraine worries, per Reuters, while the Fed's Barkin said he would 'have to be convinced' of the need for a half-point hike. [[n0122]] [[n1349]] Bloomberg reports Treasury market liquidity eroding with the Fed's course a gamble, so a hawkish surprise could move yields in gaps. [[n2210]] Politics adds noise, with Republicans delaying the vote on Biden's Fed nominees, per Politico. [[n2209]]
Playbook ✓

Action: hold a moderate equity overweight in financials, materials and selected cyclicals, funded from long-duration Treasuries and utilities. Trigger: keep it while the VIX holds below Tuesday's 25.70 and the S&P 500 stays above 4,471.07 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15); add if the 2Y stalls near 1.58% while equities hold. What changes the call: a renewed escalation that reverses the VIX's 2.63-point drop, or official support for a half-point March hike that pushes the 2Y meaningfully above 1.58%, would turn us Bearish and back toward short-dated cash and quality defensives.

geo.label: ECB gradualism versus a gas shock
parts: Macro Stance

Europe rallied harder than its fundamentals improved. The STOXX Europe 600 rose +1.43% to 467.56 index points, the DAX +1.98% to 15,412.71 index points and the CAC 40 +1.86% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15), after Putin told Germany's Scholz 'we don't want war in Europe', according to DW. [[n1320]] Yet the STOXX 600 is still -2.55% over 20 sessions, so the relief only partly repairs the January de-rating, and Europe remains the region most exposed to the energy channel of the standoff. Stance Mixed.
Activity & Inflation

The energy shock is the inflation story. Dutch TTF gas fell -12.20% to 70.92 EUR/MWh on Tuesday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15), after European energy prices had jumped on mounting tension over Ukraine, per the Luxembourg Times. [[n1311]] Putin also said Nord Stream 2 would cement Europe's energy security, Reuters reported, a reminder that supply remains a bargaining chip. [[n1330]] Eurostat documented energy prices on the rise in the euro area through 2021, and Reuters examined Europe's options in case of a Russian gas disruption. [[n2106]] [[n1336]]
New / Most Important

Policy is not racing to help. Lagarde repeated her pledge for a gradual policy shift, per Reuters, and told Bloomberg the ECB will act at the 'right time' but only gradually. [[n1309]] [[n1316]] A Reuters report put the deposit rate at -0.25% by year-end, and Reuters also argued that for euro zone bond markets the ECB 'put' is some way off, so peripheral bonds lack an explicit backstop if core yields keep climbing. [[n1308]] [[n1270]]
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer European cyclicals with pricing power, autos and industrials, over rate-sensitive defensives, and keep the energy tail hedged through gas-linked exposure rather than index shorts. Trigger: keep it while TTF stays below 78.33 EUR/MWh, its level 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). What changes the call: a renewed gas spike or an explicit supply disruption would make us Bearish on European equities relative to the US.

geo.label: Easing bias, property drag
parts: Macro Stance

China is easing while the US tightens, and that divergence is now the core of the call. Bloomberg reported the PBOC pumping in more liquidity and spurring gains in Chinese stocks. [[n0251]] The Shanghai Composite closed +0.50% at 3,446.09 index points on Tuesday but is still -3.40% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). Reuters noted the yuan slipping as divergent China-U.S. monetary policy exerts downward pressure, which is the price of that easing. [[n0267]] Stance Mixed: policy is supportive at the margin, but property stress, Omicron in Hong Kong and widening trade frictions keep the earnings recovery uncertain.
PMIs & Activity

The activity data entering February were soft at the factory gate. Reuters reported January factory activity contracting as COVID lockdowns bit, on the Caixin PMI. [[n0166]] The 2021 base was strong: Global Times reported GDP growth of 8.1%, the fastest in a decade, and Macau Business put fixed-asset investment up 4.9% for the year. [[n0150]] [[n0152]] China Daily reported industrial profits rebounding in 2021 as production improved. [[n0164]] The problem is momentum rather than level, and China Briefing's outline of infrastructure investment in 2022 shows where Beijing expects the offset to come from. [[n0214]] The next CPI and PPI prints will show whether easing producer prices give the PBOC more room.
Credit Impulse

Credit is the most constructive signal. Reuters reported Chinese government bond yields rising on faster January credit growth, a sign that the policy pipe is starting to transmit. [[n0193]] That follows January's cuts: CNBC reported the PBOC lowering key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly two years, and Fibre2Fashion reported cuts to medium-term loan and reverse repo rates. [[n0156]] [[n0159]] Bloomberg framed it as the central bank seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes. [[n0161]] The discipline remains: the South China Morning Post reported Beijing telling banks to support rural infrastructure without adding to hidden debt, which caps how far credit can be pushed through local-government channels. [[n0240]]
Property

Property remains the drag. Reuters reported Evergrande aiming to deliver 600,000 apartments in 2022 with no fire sales, and Caixin reported the developer vowing to finish half of the units it has under construction this year. [[n0181]] [[n0201]] Governance damage persists, with the WSJ reporting that Evergrande's CEO sold bonds before a profit warning. [[n0199]] Contagion has not stopped either: Bloomberg, citing Caixin, reported Cedar unable to pay $3.1 billion overdue. [[n0241]] The policy offset is incremental, with Reuters reporting property firms given easier access to escrow funds. [[n0192]] Nikkei Asia's concrete 'ghost towns' make the overhang visible. [[n0180]] We read escrow relief as liquidity triage for completions, not the start of a demand recovery.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Trade frictions are widening on several fronts. Reuters reported China suspending Lithuanian beef, dairy and beer imports as the Taiwan row grows, and Politico Europe reported Taiwan, Canada and Japan asking to join the EU's WTO case against China. [[n0195]] [[n1419]] India added 54 more Chinese apps to its ban list, Reuters reported, with Sea saying it complies with laws. [[n0850]] On the US side, the Peterson Institute found China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports in Trump's trade deal, which weakens the case for tariff relief. [[n0172]] Geopolitically, the South China Morning Post reported Beijing saying Western sanctions on Russia will worsen the Ukraine crisis, a stance that could keep secondary-sanctions risk in view for Chinese exporters. [[n1505]]
Markets & Flows

US-listed China traded the relief better than Hong Kong. In New York, KWEB rose +4.22%, the Alibaba ADR +3.54% to 126.24 USD and NIO +8.41%, while the Hang Seng slipped -0.82% to 24,355.71 index points and Tencent -0.42% to 446.40 HKD in their own session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). CNBC reported investment banks from Credit Suisse to Goldman Sachs saying it is time to buy Chinese stocks. [[n0260]] Positioning evidence is mixed, with Caixin reporting Hillhouse gobbling up shares in new-energy-vehicle makers while ditching Alibaba and Bilibili. [[n0877]] Hong Kong is the local drag, with Reuters reporting the city 'overwhelmed' as COVID infections hit a record. [[n0244]]
New / Most Important

The new signal is a sell-side turning constructive while Hong Kong's zero-COVID strain deepens. The WSJ reported Hong Kong hospital wards overflowing as Omicron defies zero-COVID policies, and Al Jazeera reported small businesses brought to their knees. [[n0261]] [[n0245]] That makes the rally in US-listed ADRs a bet on policy over epidemiology. Standard Chartered's Hong Kong unit qualifying as a direct offshore participant in CIPS, China's cross-border payment system, per Reuters, is a small plumbing signal that may matter more if Western sanctions on Russia come into force. [[n0235]]
Playbook ✓

Action: keep a tactical, small long in China internet and NEV ADRs (KWEB, the Alibaba ADR, NIO), paired against an underweight in property-exposed credit. Trigger: hold while the Shanghai Composite stays above 3,446.09 index points and KWEB above 37.81 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15); add only if the next credit data confirm January's acceleration. What changes the call: another developer payment failure of Cedar's kind, or a Hong Kong lockdown escalation that pushes Tencent below its 20-session reference of 438.07 HKD. ⚠ Divergence: Western banks are calling China a buy and the PBOC is injecting liquidity, yet the yuan is slipping, Hong Kong's hospitals are overflowing and developers are still missing payments; the policy signal and the earnings signal point in opposite directions.

geo.label: GDP rebound, BOJ patience
parts: Macro Stance

Japan's macro is better than its market. Reuters reported the economy rebounding on solid spending, with Omicron clouding the outlook. [[n1552]] Equities did not reward it: the Nikkei 225 fell -0.79% to 26,865.19 index points on Tuesday and is -5.18% over 20 sessions, with Tokyo Electron -2.40% and Sony Group -2.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). Tokyo closed before the US relief session, which showed up only in EWJ's +1.11% in New York. Stance Mixed: domestic demand is recovering, but the export-heavy index carries chip, auto and energy-cost drag.
Activity & Currency

The weak links are autos and real wages. Automotive Logistics reported Toyota cutting March production plans because of the chip shortage, and Toyota Motor shares are -11.12% over 20 sessions at 2,153.50 JPY (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). [[n1978]] The Japan Times explained why wages aren't rising, which keeps the BOJ patient, even after Reuters reported the BOJ debating its messaging on an eventual rate hike as inflation perks up. [[n1529]] [[n1514]] That policy gap versus a hiking Fed is the currency channel: the yen's haven role on Ukraine scares competes with a widening rate differential that tends to weaken it. Imports hitting record highs on surging energy prices, as The Seattle Times reported, make the terms-of-trade squeeze visible and explain why a cheaper yen is less of a gift than it used to be. [[n1517]]
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight Japanese autos (Toyota Motor) relative to Japanese chip-equipment names (Tokyo Electron, Advantest), which have more operating leverage to a semiconductor relief rally. Trigger: keep the Toyota underweight while it trades below 2,423.00 JPY, its level 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15), and rotate into the equipment names when they confirm the US chip rally in local trading. What changes the call: evidence that chip supply to carmakers is easing would flip us to Bullish on Toyota; a BOJ signal of earlier tightening would hurt both legs through a stronger yen.

geo.label: QE ended, hike debate open
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is a policy-transition story. The SMH reported the RBA ending QE with a murky future for $650b of assets, following Governor Philip Lowe's February monetary policy decision statement. [[n0033]] [[n0016]] The S&P/ASX 200 fell -0.51% to 7,206.90 index points on Tuesday and is -2.84% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). ABC reported Fortescue Metals and CSL posting weaker profits from COVID-19 restrictions, and Fortescue fell -5.10% to 21.59 AUD. [[n0066]] Stance Mixed.
Demand & Financing

Labour and inflation argue for earlier hikes. The Australian reported the jobless rate hitting a 13-year low as an RBA hike looms, and the AFR reported a shock inflation spike to 3.5 per cent. [[n0004]] [[n0009]] The AFR also flagged rising rents as the sleeper factor for inflation. [[n0040]] Banks see the upside: The Australian reported CBA bullish on the economy as rate hikes loom, and CBA shares are +5.50% over five sessions at 99.49 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). [[n0291]] The Guardian warned supply-chain issues are likely to continue despite a drop in COVID cases. [[n0053]] Spending and capital are both still flowing: the AFR reported JB Hi-Fi shares jumping on a capital return and a sales lift, and Reuters reported Crown Resorts backing a $6.3 billion Blackstone bid. [[n1173]] [[n0654]]
Playbook ✓

Action: favour Australian banks (CBA) over iron-ore pure plays (Fortescue). Trigger: hold while CBA stays above 99.49 AUD and Fortescue fails to recover Tuesday's -5.10% loss (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). What changes the call: an RBA push-back against early-hike expectations would hurt the bank leg, and a Chinese property stimulus surprise that revives iron ore would hurt the short leg.

geo.label: Hawkish NBP versus border risk
parts: Macro Stance

Poland's macro picture is an inflation shock met by an increasingly hawkish central bank, with a geopolitical premium layered on top. Forsal reported the statistics office putting January inflation at 9.2%, and the Association of Individual Investors (SII) stressed it stayed below 10% while still the highest of this century. [[n1788]] [[n1790]] The Monetary Policy Council has already lifted rates to the highest in almost nine years, Rzeczpospolita reported, and NBP President Adam Glapiński cast himself as a hawk at an unusual press conference, according to Interia. [[n1618]] [[n1622]] Stance Mixed: the tightening is credible and the złoty has responded, but real incomes are being squeezed while the country sits next to the standoff.
Markets

Polish assets rebounded hard on the pullback news. The iShares MSCI Poland ETF (EPOL) jumped +5.46% to 21.24 USD and the Beta ETF WIG20TR tracker +2.09% to 38.07 PLN, with mBank +5.66% to 485.60 PLN and PKO Bank Polski +1.90% to 47.27 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). Over 20 sessions EPOL is still -3.32% and the WIG20TR tracker -6.46%, so the rally has not erased January's damage. On the currency, Bankier reported the złoty at its strongest in eight months and credited Glapiński's comments for the move, before reporting the złoty recovering losses as the Ukraine issue hit markets. [[n1672]] [[n1645]] [[n1770]] Parkiet argued bank quotes on the Warsaw exchange have potential to extend their bull run, while Bankier asked whether the market is still in correction or already in a bear phase. [[n1678]] [[n1664]] Retirement savers felt it, with Analizy reporting every PPK vintage negative in January. [[n1759]]
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal metrics flatter, politics does not. Rzeczpospolita reported the 2021 central budget deficit at 26.3 billion złoty, and Bankier relayed the finance ministry's estimate of the same figure. [[n1694]] [[n1702]] Rzeczpospolita also argued inflation is helping the government cope with its debt. [[n1617]] The Polski Ład tax reform is the political liability: Business Insider Polska reported Jan Sarnowski, who was responsible for it, losing his post, and Polsat News tied the deputy finance minister's dismissal to the reform's problems. [[n1701]] [[n1698]] Parkiet described a marginalised finance minister inside the PiS government, and Interia carried a poll on whether Polski Ład has damaged Law and Justice. [[n1743]] [[n1760]] Spending pressure is rising, with Rzeczpospolita reporting pension indexation higher than forecast and 300Gospodarka saying it will cost more than the budget assumed. [[n1653]] [[n1713]] In Brussels, EUobserver said a rule-of-law judgment is seen piling pressure on von der Leyen, a ruling that could bear on Poland's access to EU funds. [[n1585]]
Corporate & Sectors

Energy and resources dominate the corporate tape. Orlen rose +3.83% to 73.28 PLN, KGHM +2.19% to 154.00 PLN and coking-coal miner JSW +5.56% to 48.00 PLN, the latter +19.40% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). Parkiet reported Jacek Sasin and KGHM heading to the US for small nuclear reactors, and eKoszalin reported KGHM targeting SMRs in Poland as early as 2029. [[n1738]] [[n1795]] Utilities are repositioning: WNP said Tauron bought CO2 allowances at 30 euro and locked in a fixed interest rate, and netka.gda.pl reported PGE's Baltica 3 offshore wind stage of about 1045 MW planned for 2026. [[n1656]] [[n1737]] In consumer names, CD Projekt released the next-generation update of Cyberpunk 2077 with a free trial, per its investor-relations site, while Dino Polska jumped +5.15% to 296.00 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). [[n1776]] Housing stays firm, with Strefa Inwestorów reporting apartment prices still rising in the fourth quarter after double-digit gains across 2021. [[n1782]]
Geopolitics & Security

Warsaw is on the front line diplomatically and militarily. Poland, as OSCE chair, has said political will is needed to end the standoff, Reuters reported, and Foreign Minister Rau told TVN24 after talks with Lavrov in Moscow that European security is in deep crisis, while Fakt reported Lavrov speaking of 'information terrorism'. [[n1566]] [[n1804]] [[n1801]] Reuters reported the US sending 3,000 additional troops to Poland, and CNBC reported US troops there preparing to help refugees if Russia invades Ukraine. [[n1580]] [[n1586]] Rzeczpospolita, citing Reuters, reported Ukrainian veterans in Poland saying they would return to fight if Russia attacks. [[n1763]] Energy security is the economic transmission: the Energy Regulatory Office reported a record price for gas imported from EU countries in the last quarter of 2021, and Biznes Alert quoted Woźniak rejecting a new Yamal contract with Russia. [[n1762]] [[n1768]] Money.pl reported businesses alarmed by letters announcing gas supply restrictions. [[n1682]]
New / Most Important

The new information is that inflation has pushed through 9% just as Russia claims a partial pullback. Bankier reported inflation exceeding 9%, and 300Gospodarka asked whether January's renewed rise marks the peak of the sharp price gains. [[n1791]] [[n1792]] Glapiński has said Poland must live with higher inflation, per Super Biznes, and Polsat News carried a rate-setter's pledge to keep urging tighter monetary policy as loan instalments rise, which keeps the rate path hawkish into spring. [[n1651]] [[n1648]] The NBP also plans to buy another 100 tonnes of gold, Business Insider Polska reported, a reserve move that fits a central bank hedging geopolitical risk. [[n1624]] For markets the mix supports banks and the złoty but squeezes savers, and Obserwator Gospodarczy explained why deposit rates are not rising. [[n1785]]
Playbook ✓

Action: overweight Polish banks (PKO Bank Polski, mBank) against an underweight in rate-sensitive consumer names, and keep złoty exposure unhedged only while de-escalation holds. Trigger: keep the bank overweight while EPOL holds above 21.24 USD and mBank above 485.60 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15); add on a further hawkish Monetary Policy Council decision. What changes the call: a collapse of Moscow's pullback claim, or a dovish NBP turn, would push us to Bearish on Polish assets as a whole. ⚠ Divergence: the NBP is hawkish and banks are rallying, but Poland is receiving US troop reinforcements for a crisis that markets just repriced as easing, gas import prices are at records and the Polski Ład turmoil is eroding fiscal credibility; a strong złoty and a frontline security position cannot both persist if the pullback is not verified.
Narrative

Technology led the relief: XLK rose +2.63% to 158.91 USD, with Apple +2.32% and Microsoft +1.85%, but it remains -1.77% over 20 sessions with the 10Y at 2.05% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-15). The sector is trading the discount rate, not earnings.
Reported

Deal flow is the reported news. Intel agreed to acquire Tower Semiconductor for $5.4 billion, per Intel's investor-relations release, and the WSJ reported Cisco made a $20 billion-plus takeover offer for Splunk. [[n0851]] [[n1138]] CRN reported Lenovo topping HP and Dell in the best year for PC shipments in a decade, per IDC. [[n0855]]
EPS Upside Watch

Upside sits in infrastructure software and security, where Cloudflare is +23.20% and Datadog +28.15% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15); a beat-and-raise pattern there would confirm that enterprise budgets survive higher rates. If the 10Y stabilises, multiples stop being the marginal driver and revisions take over.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The contrarian read is that M&A, not multiple expansion, is the sector's real tell: acquirers paying up for Tower and pursuing Splunk signal that strategic buyers see value after the January drawdown, a floor-building signal that momentum flows cannot provide.
Narrative

Communication services is the weakest large sector on fundamentals. XLC rose +1.40% to 70.29 USD on Tuesday but is -7.06% over 20 sessions, and Meta Platforms (FB) sits at 221.00 USD, -30.54% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). Forbes put a $10 billion figure on the impact of privacy changes across Apple and Meta. [[n0416]]
Reported

Reuters reported Facebook paying $90 million to settle a privacy lawsuit over user tracking, and Al Jazeera reported Texas suing Meta over facial recognition. [[n0861]] [[n0762]] Disney was the exception, with Reuters reporting streaming growth and park revenue boosting the shares. [[n0311]]
EPS Upside Watch

Upside is concentrated where pricing power is visible: Walt Disney is +8.59% over five sessions while Netflix is -20.23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15), so investors are paying for parks-plus-streaming cash flow over pure subscriber growth. ViacomCBS renaming itself Paramount to underscore its streaming future, per CNBC, tests the same thesis. [[n1999]]
⚡ Breaking Convention

Narrative

Financials are the cleanest beneficiary of a Fed hiking into a positively sloped curve. XLF rose +1.36% to 40.20 USD, KRE +2.68%, and Morgan Stanley is +10.02% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). The 3M at 0.40% against a 10Y at 2.05% leaves a +165 bps spread for deposit-funded lenders (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-15).
Reported

Abroad, CNBC reported Singapore's DBS profit rebounding and seen gaining as the rates outlook improves, and The Australian reported CBA's Mike Vacy Lyle saying bullish banks see a brighter outlook. [[n1955]] [[n0657]] Kansas City Fed research on how net interest margins at small and large banks vary with rates frames the mechanism. [[n2174]]
EPS Upside Watch

Upside comes from net interest income at regional lenders as March lift-off lands. The risk is the flattening itself: the 2Y has risen 52 bps against 18 bps for the 10Y over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-15), which compresses long-dated lending margins if it continues.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Conduct risk is the overlooked drag: the WSJ reported regulators probing block trading at Morgan Stanley, Goldman and other Wall Street firms. [[n0723]] Investment-bank earnings could therefore lag balance-sheet banks even as rates rise, so we prefer KRE to brokers.
Narrative

Energy is where the geopolitical premium is being repriced in real time. Reuters reported oil hitting seven-year highs as the market feared an imminent Russian attack on Ukraine; then Brent fell -3.32% to 93.28 USD/bbl, WTI -3.55% to 92.07 USD/bbl and XLE -1.05% to 68.03 USD on Tuesday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). [[n0128]]
Reported

Fundamentals stay tight: Reuters reported an IEA demand revision confirming a tighter oil market, and The Intercept reported Saudi Arabia rejecting Biden's plea to increase output. [[n0765]] [[n1995]] Morningstar explained why energy stocks are gushing high dividends. [[n0395]]
EPS Upside Watch

Upside remains in cash returns even at lower crude: XLE is still +5.03% over 20 sessions and Exxon Mobil +6.72%. Oilfield services may lead next, with Schlumberger rising +2.01% on the day while integrated majors fell (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15).

The overlooked supply swing is Iran, not Russia: Reuters reported Iran's oil exports increasing as nuclear talks resume, and a deal would cap crude even if Ukraine flares. [[n1399]] Barron's list of energy stocks that shorts are betting against shows the sector already carries a bearish cohort that can fuel squeezes. [[n0528]]

Industrials rose +1.51% to 100.48 USD but remain -3.97% over 20 sessions; Boeing gained +3.66% while Caterpillar is -11.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). Aerospace demand is recovering faster than heavy-machinery sentiment.

[[n0914]] [[n0913]]

Upside sits in aerospace aftermarket and grid capex, with Quanta Services +5.41% and Eaton +2.21% on Tuesday. [[n0664]]
⚡ Breaking Convention

[[n0784]] [[n0785]] Burger King's parent topped estimates on digital sales growth, per CNBC, while Forbes reported Peloton shares falling after its new CEO said the company won't be sold in the foreseeable future. [[n1193]] [[n0747]]

⚡ Breaking Convention

earnings_pattern.title: Guidance beats the print; pandemic winners lose the benefit of the doubt
parts: Rewarded

Companies that paired results with durable forward demand were paid. Airbnb published fourth-quarter and full-year 2021 results, and Al Jazeera reported the company seeing strong first-quarter revenue on a travel resurgence, after the stock had already risen +6.14% to 180.07 USD into the report (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). [[n1190]] [[n0785]] GeekWire reported Zillow shares up 16% as it revealed a 'housing super app' strategy amid the iBuying closure, and MarketWatch reported Twitter swinging to a gain after underwhelming user growth because of a new $4 billion buyback. [[n0511]] [[n0491]] TechCrunch reported Disney+ outshining Netflix with 11.8M new subscribers and a strong forecast. [[n1106]]
Punished

The punished group is pandemic-era growth losing its narrative. Reuters reported Roblox quarterly bookings disappointing as the gaming frenzy wanes, and The Business Journals reported a big after-hours stock drop. [[n0883]] [[n0880]] CNBC reported Delivery Hero's CEO apologising to investors after a 30% stock plunge, and Reuters reported Uber's 2024 profit forecast falling short of expectations and the shares dropping. [[n0550]] [[n0494]] BioPharma Dive reported Seagen shares sinking as the sales outlook for a cancer drug disappointed, showing guidance, not the quarter, sets the reaction. [[n1125]]
Pattern

The market rewards evidence of durable demand and punishes extrapolated lockdown demand. Travel, resources and capital returns get credit; gaming, delivery and home fitness lose it. MarketWatch's list of 15 stocks that rose 100% or more during the pandemic but have since been crushed is the template for the punished cohort. [[n0638]] Costs matter less than volume: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo warned of an inflation bite yet higher prices lifted sales, and the market has so far accepted price-led growth. [[n1137]]
Attention into EPS

Attention ran into the print in metaverse and gaming names, which raised the bar: Roblox rallied +7.29% in its last session before results and +13.77% over five sessions, then disappointed (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). The New York Times' report of Meta and Salesforce presenting differing takes on the metaverse shows the theme is now contested rather than consensus, so crowded pre-earnings positioning is a liability. [[n0111]]
Playbook

Fade pre-earnings run-ups in names whose bull case rests on lockdown engagement, and buy post-earnings dips only where guidance improves, as at Airbnb. Trigger: a stock that outruns its sector over five sessions into results without a guidance catalyst. What changes the call: a broad upturn in earnings revisions for growth software would make pre-earnings momentum safer to hold.

Bitcoin's 20-session gain contrasts with the Nasdaq 100's -3.88% over the same span, so crypto has stopped trading as a leveraged copy of growth equities for now. CNBC framed the outlook for bitcoin around geopolitical tensions and rising interest rates, the two forces that briefly moved in crypto's favour. [[n2198]]
New / Most Important

The industry's Super Bowl blitz is the new data point. Bloomberg said the ad blitz told Americans to stop worrying and just buy crypto, CNN reported Coinbase's QR-code ad briefly crashing its app, and Reuters reported Coinbase shares slipping as a result. [[n0761]] [[n0709]] [[n0708]] The Seattle Times reported the crypto millions spent on Super Bowl ads didn't drive downloads, and WIRED said the ads feel like Pets.com all over again, a comparison to an earlier era of advertising-led hype. [[n1015]] [[n0957]] Value money is circling the miners, with CNBC reporting Bill Miller calling bitcoin miners very attractively valued. [[n0946]]
Playbook

Action: hold core bitcoin exposure but do not chase high-beta miners and altcoins after one relief day. Trigger: add only if bitcoin holds above 44,575.20 USD while the 2Y yield stops rising from 1.58% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-15). What changes the call: a hawkish Fed surprise or renewed escalation would hit crypto as a risk asset rather than a haven, and a slide back toward 36,852.12 USD would mark the relief as failed.

flows.title: Liquidity drains at the core while money hunts for income
parts: Global Liquidity

Global liquidity is moving in opposite directions. A Reuters commentary argued a historic central-bank drain calls the 'buy the dip' reflex into question, and the FT reported markets losing trust in central banks. [[n1347]] [[n1341]] The tightening camp is broad: Barron's reported the Bank of England hiking for a second time in a row while the ECB stayed put, and the SMH reported Australia ending QE. [[n1250]] [[n0033]] China is the lone large injector, with Bloomberg reporting the PBOC pumping in more liquidity, and India is holding steady, with The Week reporting the RBI keeping its repo rate unchanged at 4%. [[n0251]] [[n1348]] Al Jazeera reported emerging markets dreading deja vu as Fed hikes loom, the classic channel by which a shrinking Fed balance sheet tightens conditions abroad. [[n2153]] Sir Jon Cunliffe's Bank of England speech on learning from the dash for cash and on margining practices is a reminder that forced selling, not valuation, is what turns tightening into a liquidity event. [[n1265]] For global portfolios the net effect is less central-bank balance sheet, which raises the cost of leverage and favours assets that pay cash now.
Rates & Dollar

The dollar is not the stress channel yet. DXY ended at 95.99 index points, -0.39% on Tuesday and only +0.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). The stress sits in rates: the 2Y's 52 bps 20-observation rise against 18 bps for the 10Y is the bear flattening (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-15). Reuters' explainer on why the flattening of the US yield curve matters spells out the growth signal investors are watching, and Bloomberg reported Treasury market liquidity eroding. [[n2176]] [[n2210]] The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget asked how higher interest rates would affect federal interest payments, the fiscal side of the same repricing. [[n2181]] Dealer capacity matters: a Richmond Fed study of how post-2008 financial regulations affected corporate bond liquidity is relevant when balance sheets must absorb a repricing. [[n1345]]
Credit Check

Credit is softening, not breaking. HYG rose +0.17% to 82.66 USD but is -3.51% over 20 sessions, LQD is -3.77% and EMB -0.79% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15); investment grade has lost more than high yield because duration, not default, is the driver. Artemis reported insurance bonds showing resilience as spreads reset, citing Twelve Capital, and 9fin's leveraged-finance wrap described paltry primary issuance serving up more floating-rate deals, a sign borrowers and buyers are both avoiding fixed-rate duration. [[n1369]] [[n1275]] The default pocket is Chinese property, where Bloomberg reported Cedar unable to pay $3.1 billion overdue. [[n0241]]
Equity & Fund Flows

The flow evidence favours income over duration. Reuters reported US dividend funds receiving huge inflows as investors switch out of bonds, and Morningstar explained why inflation-protected bond funds are losing money. [[n1344]] [[n1360]] Hedging is active, with Bloomberg reporting a big options trade hedging an S&P 500 plunge of up to 20% by April. [[n2196]] Quarter-end filings show large holders rotating: CNBC reported Buffett increasing an energy bet by more than a third, Business Insider reported Michael Burry exiting CVS Health in the fourth quarter, and the Mormon Church's $52 billion stock fund added Tesla while trimming Ford and GM. [[n0728]] [[n0674]] [[n0738]] The Straits Times reported Temasek adding stakes in Grab, Robinhood and other consumer-focused companies. [[n1853]] Primary markets are selective: CNBC reported India's Life Insurance Corporation filing for an $8 billion IPO, while Reuters reported the Atlantic Coastal SPAC scrapping its merger with Essentium and Syniverse and M3-Brigade scrapping theirs. [[n1362]] [[n1358]] [[n1343]]
Portfolio Implication

Keep equity risk but change its composition: favour dividend payers, financials and materials, funded from long-duration bonds and investment-grade credit, which carry the bear-flattening risk. Hold index puts rather than excess cash as the geopolitical hedge, since the relief rally has cut implied volatility, and keep emerging-market duration light while the Fed's start is unresolved. The Economist's question of what would happen if financial markets crashed is the right stress test: the portfolio should survive a disorderly repricing without forced sales. [[n1304]] What changes the call: a dollar breakout above its 20-session range combined with high-yield losses accelerating beyond investment grade would signal genuine liquidity stress and justify cutting gross equity exposure.

anticipatory.title: March FOMC: quarter point or half point

parts: Catalyst & Thesis

ABC reported Fortescue Metals posting weaker profits from COVID-19 restrictions. [[n0066]] Thesis: Fortescue is a pure iron-ore exposure tied to Chinese steel and property, and Reuters reported China's 2021 iron ore imports retreating from a record on steel curbs. [[n0144]] Al Jazeera reported Western Australia's border limbo sparking production fears, an operating risk on top of price risk. [[n0047]]
Price Hurdle & Risk

Shares fell -5.10% to 21.59 AUD but remain +3.95% over 20 sessions, so the de-rating has room to run (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). Risk: a Chinese property stimulus surprise, or tighter seaborne supply after Mining Weekly reported Vale producing less iron than expected. [[n0051]]
Trade Expression
Underweight against BHP, whose first-half profit beat estimates, per Reuters; cover if Fortescue recovers Tuesday's -5.10% loss (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-15). [[n0691]]
